All 95 phrase pairs read against the complete original paragraph. All nine full primary contexts were read, retaining both Sanhedrin metaphors, Rashi’s interpretation of Rabbi Yochanan, the complete Sukkah sequence, Beit Hillel’s concrete conduct, the legal context of the two names, the limited Yochanan chronology, and both narratives of celebratory lighting. Read back the corrections to craftsmen and smiths and the mil measured from the city. The unresolved abbreviation לק״ל remains visible without an invented expansion; the proposed nusach OCR reading is disclosed, and the malicious report in Eikhah Rabbah is distinguished from the Jews’ actual observance. Continuation review: every phrase and note translation read; English bracket conventions removed without deleting meaning; all Hebrew and original snapshots preserved. Textual uncertainties remain explicitly disclosed. The malicious-report qualification remains explicit in English at phrase 87; לק״ל remains unexpanded and openly marked unresolved. The five recovered notes were independently checked against the direct primary responses: Bava Batra 172a:11–13, Mishnah Maaser Sheni 5:15, Mishneh Torah Tithes 9:1, the chronological gloss in Rash MiShantz on Mishnah Parah 3:8:2, and Zohar Achrei Mot 74:409. Seven legacy identities are accounted for once and the impossible Lamentations 4:100 duplicate is explicitly retired.
